round1_critical_status.finding: SEC-01 (critical) — tailscale_authkey leaked via argv, register, and logs
round1_critical_status.evidence: no_log: true added to the assert, `tailscale up`, and `tailscale status` tasks (tailscale/tasks/main.yml:8, 68, 94). This closes the Ansible-side log/register exposure. However, the authkey is still passed as `--authkey={{ tailscale_authkey }}` on the argv of `tailscale up` (line 59). Round 1 explicitly called out `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` / `ps auxf` exposure on the VM and recommended `tailscale up --auth-key file:/proc/self/fd/3` or env-var + stdin. That argv-level exposure is not addressed. With `retries: 3`, the key sits in cmdline for up to ~3*10s windows on every run. Anyone with `ps`/`/proc` read on the box (the `op` user with NOPASSWD: ALL trivially) can grab the key, which is reusable until Tailscale-side expiry. Treat as still-critical.

round1_critical_status.finding: RE-02 / SEC-02 (critical) — SSH hardening reload before Tailscale SSH is live (lockout)
round1_critical_status.evidence: SSH hardening tasks moved to the END of the base role (base/tasks/main.yml:100-118) with `validate: sshd -t` and `backup: true` added — addresses the parse-error brick risk and the intra-role ordering. BUT: the tailscale role still runs as a SEPARATE role AFTER base, so the handler-flush at end-of-base reloads sshd with `PermitRootLogin no` + `PasswordAuthentication no` BEFORE `tailscale up --ssh` has ever executed (the only place tailnet SSH is enabled). The fix does not add: (a) `authorized_keys` deployment for `op` before hardening, (b) cross-role re-ordering (e.g., placing hardening in a post-tailscale `harden` role), or (c) a `wait_for`/`ansible.builtin.wait_for_connection` probe against the tailnet endpoint before hardening. The original lockout class (fresh Hetzner VM bootstrapped over public-IP SSH with only root key) is unchanged. The Round 1 critical was about cross-role ordering; the fix only addressed intra-role ordering plus belt-and-braces validate/backup.

round1_critical_status.finding: RE-04 (high) — UFW deny-all enabled before tailscale0 exists (lockout window)
round1_critical_status.evidence: Commit message claims 'enable moved to be handled post-Tailscale'. In practice the explicit `Enable ufw` task is deleted, AND the bogus `policy: established,related` task is correctly removed (closes RE-07). However, the remaining `Configure ufw to allow Tailscale interface` task (base/tasks/main.yml:91-98) still carries `state: enabled` — the `community.general.ufw` module activates UFW as a side-effect when `state: enabled` is passed. So UFW is still enabled inside the base role, before the tailscale role runs, and the tailscale0 interface still does not exist at that moment. The lockout window is unchanged. No post-tailscale UFW enablement task exists anywhere; the commit message's claim of 'moved to be handled post-Tailscale' is not reflected in any committed task. If the orchestrator intended a follow-up commit/task for this, it's missing.

round1_critical_status.finding: RE-01 (critical) — auto-reboot enabled with no guard
round1_critical_status.evidence: `Unattended-Upgrade::AutoRebootTime "04:00";` removed; `Unattended-Upgrade::Automatic-Reboot "false";` added explicitly (base/files/50unattended-upgrades:10). Matches Round 1 recommendation exactly.

Round 1 recommended either `failed_when: stdout | length == 0` on the get-IP task or an explicit `assert` after set_fact. The fix adds `failed_when: tailscale_ip_cmd.stdout | length == 0` (tailscale/tasks/main.yml:82) AND removes the `when: stdout | length > 0` guard from the `set_fact` (line 84-86). Empty stdout now fails the play loudly. Recommendation satisfied.

Replaced with `changed_when: tailscale_up_result.rc == 0 and 'already' not in tailscale_up_result.stdout | lower` (tailscale/tasks/main.yml:67). Matches Round 1's first-line fix recommendation. Caveat: with `no_log: true` on this task, stdout is still evaluated correctly by Ansible internals — but operators debugging will not see the value the predicate ran on. Acceptable.

round1_critical_status.finding: SEC-02 / RE-09 (major) — apt_key deprecation + unscoped trust
round1_critical_status.evidence: Switched to `get_url` → `/usr/share/keyrings/tailscale-archive-keyring.gpg`, repo line uses `[signed-by=...]`, distro flipped from `focal` to `noble` (tailscale/tasks/main.yml:10-25). Three of the three Round 1 sub-issues (deprecation, global trust, wrong distro) addressed. The fourth sub-issue (GPG fingerprint pinning via `gpg --show-keys` check task) is still absent — acceptable as it was characterized as best-practice belt-and-braces, not the blocker.

Added `regexp: '^{{ base_operator_user }}\s'` to the sudoers lineinfile task (base/tasks/main.yml:54). Now replaces matching line instead of appending. Combined with the existing `validate: visudo -cf` (preserved), this is safe.

New variable `tailscale_accept_routes: false` in tailscale/defaults/main.yml:12 with README-equivalent warning comment. `tailscale up` now uses `{% if tailscale_accept_routes %}--accept-routes{% endif %}` inline (tailscale/tasks/main.yml:61). Default behavior is now safer.

The deeper Round 1 sub-concern about Ubuntu 24.04's `Include /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/*.conf` and recommendation to write a drop-in file is not addressed — acceptable as Round 1 marked this minor.

regressions.title: UFW activation now relies on undocumented side-effect of `state: enabled` on tailscale0 rule
regressions.detail: The explicit `Enable ufw` task was removed (good intention) but no post-tailscale UFW-enable task was added. UFW is still activated inside base role via the `state: enabled` parameter on the `Configure ufw to allow Tailscale interface` task. This is more confusing than the original code: a future contributor refactoring the rule task could silently disable UFW activation. Either drop `state: enabled` from the rule task and add an explicit ordered `Enable ufw` task after the tailscale role, or document the side-effect inline. Location: infrastructure/ansible/roles/base/tasks/main.yml:91-98.

regressions.title: `--accept-routes` jinja templating inside folded YAML scalar is brittle
regressions.detail: `tailscale/tasks/main.yml:54-62` uses `cmd: >` (folded scalar) with `{% if tailscale_accept_routes %}--accept-routes{% endif %}` on its own line. When the var is false, this collapses to a stray space, which `tailscale up` tolerates today but is non-obvious. Cleaner pattern: build the command as a list (`argv:`) or use `{{ '--accept-routes' if tailscale_accept_routes else '' }}` inline. Not a runtime defect, but a maintenance hazard.

regressions.title: Molecule `tailscale_ip` assertion masked by `ignore_errors: true`
regressions.detail: tailscale/molecule/default/verify.yml:48 carries `ignore_errors: true` on the new `tailscale_ip` assertion. This perpetuates the same antipattern that RE-08 flagged. Better: split into a check-mode-aware probe that fails the verify when the role-converge has finished and `tailscale_ip` is missing (i.e., remove `ignore_errors`, gate the assertion behind `when: tailscale_up_result is not skipped`).

blocking_issues_remaining: SEC-01: authkey still in argv (/proc/<pid>/cmdline) — switch to env-var or `--auth-key file:` to truly close

RE-02: SSH hardening still reloads sshd before tailscale role runs `tailscale up --ssh` — add a `wait_for_connection`/`wait_for` probe on the tailnet endpoint, deploy `authorized_keys` for `op`, or move hardening to a post-tailscale `harden` role
RE-04: UFW still implicitly activated in base role; either add explicit post-tailscale enable task or document and pin the side-effect
rationale: Round 2 closed 3/3 high findings, 2/2 major findings, and the bulk of medium/minor work — solid progress. However, two of the three Round 1 critical findings (SEC-01 authkey-in-argv, RE-02 cross-role SSH lockout) are only partially addressed and one high (RE-04 UFW ordering) was reshuffled rather than fixed. The lockout-class issues are the same failure mode Round 1 called out as merge blockers. Recommend one focused fix pass: (a) move authkey off argv (env or stdin), (b) deploy authorized_keys for `op` before SSH hardening AND add a `wait_for_connection` probe on the tailnet endpoint OR split hardening into a post-tailscale role, (c) add an explicit `Enable ufw` task that runs after the tailscale role completes. Estimated < 1 hour of work. Do not merge until lockout-class issues are closed — a single bad bootstrap run still bricks the VM.
